summary: Pinned-model lease extended by liveness-retry activity blocks canary cutover for tenant 'acme-analytics'
description:
Issue summary:

During a weighted canary cutover for tenant 'acme-analytics' the pinned-model lease for the tenant was repeatedly extended by liveness-probe retry responses coming from an edge healthcheck path. As a result the canary coordinator was unable to commit the cutover (commit window repeatedly deferred) and tenant traffic remained on the legacy variant for ~45 minutes.

Impact:
- Tenant Acme Analytics saw no traffic migrate to the canary variant for a scheduled 30% rollout during the maintenance window.
- Observable increase in request cost due to repeated prewarm attempts and repeated KV-cache reservations for the legacy variant.
- User-facing: three customer-reported degraded responses and one billing inquiry.

Environment:
- prod cluster: us-west (us-west-2)
- Route: /v1/chat/tenant/acme-analytics
- Canary config: weighted rollout 30% (variant-c), legacy variant (variant-a) pinned until commit
- Orchestrator version: 2026.02.7
- Serving runtime build: rwinfer-serving-2026.02.3

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Start a staged weighted rollout (30%) via console for tenant route.
2. Canary coordinator initiates prewarm on variant-c and emits canary-health probes to edge-probe.
3. During prewarm there was an intermittent 502 from one edge-probe instance; edge healthcheck logic retried the liveness probe path and each retry included a sticky session header which the routing-mesh treated as a keepalive-affinity update.
4. The orchestrator's pin-manager observed activity on the legacy variant and extended the pinned-model TTL (grace window) rather than allowing commit to proceed.
5. Canary commit attempts were deferred until the pin TTL expired; repeated probe retries extended the TTL multiple times, preventing cutover.

Expected behavior:
- Liveness/retry probing should not extend tenant pin leases. Retry activity from healthcheck endpoints should be treated as non-affinity traffic and not update pin TTL. The canary coordinator should be able to complete the cutover once prewarm success is declared or after a bounded commit backoff.

Observed behavior:
- Pin-manager increments TTL on certain probe/keepalive events when the probe carried a stale affinity header. Repeated probe retries lead to pin TTL being extended beyond the coordinator's commit window, blocking canary traffic migration.

Relevant logs and telemetry pointers:
- Routing mesh logs (trace id): rm:trace-20260313-7f9b
- Orchestrator audit events: /var/log/orchestrator/commits/2026-03-13.log lines 512-578
- Pin-manager metrics: pin_lease_extension_count{route="acme-analytics",region="us-west"} spikes at 2026-03-13T22:12Z
- Edge-probe logs (pod edge-probe-3): ERROR 502 -> healthcheck retry at 2026-03-13T22:11:58Z
- Console timeline event: rollout_attempt_id=roll-20260313-acme-01

Temporary workaround applied:
- Support instructed to toggle canary coordinator to force-commit with ignore-pin flag (internal operator action) which completed rollout for this tenant while we investigate. This is documented in the rollout audit (see related_confluence_pages).

Customer-visible communications:
- Customer CS notified at 2026-03-13T23:04Z. Customer requested a post-mortem and billing credit evaluation for redundant prewarm costs.
comments: 2026-03-13 23:00 - Maya Patel (Support): Initial triage complete. Observed pin_lease_extension_count spike. Escalating to SRE. Logged sup ticket SUP-7777777.

2026-03-13 23:17 - Diego Morales (SRE): Reproduced locally by replaying edge-probe retries against a shadow route. Pin-manager increments TTL on 'X-Tenant-Affinity' header even for healthcheck paths. Working on mitigations.
2026-03-13 23:45 - Diego Morales (SRE): Applied operator 'force-commit ignore-pin' to finish customer cutover as temporary mitigation. Notifying customer and scheduling follow-up patch.

2026-03-14 08:30 - Priya Singh (Eng, orchestrator): Added hypothesis that probe retries are treated as activity because of header normalization change in routing-mesh v2.1. Creating PR to add probe-path filter to pin-manager. See PR linked.
2026-03-14 12:10 - Maya Patel (Support): Customer acknowledged temporary rollback; requested ETA for permanent fix and confirmation that billing credits will be evaluated.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: Routing mesh forwarded healthcheck requests with sticky-session header causing pin-manager to interpret them as active sessions.
Hypothesis B: A recent change in edge-probe added retry behavior that sets 'X-Tenant-Affinity' on retries; earlier behavior omitted it.
Reproducible when replaying probes with header present; not reproducible when header stripped.

Pin-manager code path: pin_lease_extend() is invoked when incoming request metadata contains affinity or KVcache reservation signals. Need to add explicit healthcheck route detection and ignore extension in that path.
next_steps: Ship PR to add healthcheck-path exclusion in pin-manager (target: 2026-03-15 deployment).
Patch edge-probe to avoid emitting affinity headers on retries (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-probe/pull/225).
Post-mortem & billing evaluation with CS and Finance (owner: Maya Patel).
Add automated test to replay healthcheck retries to prevent regressions.
resolution: In progress – temporary operator force-commit allowed customer cutover. Engineering patch in progress to ensure liveness probes and retry traffic do not extend pin TTL. Full fix targeted for 2026-03-15 deployment.
resolution_notes: Operator mitigation used: canary coordinator forced commit with ignore-pin flag at 2026-03-13T23:45Z.
Customer cutover completed at 2026-03-13T23:50Z; customer confirmed canary traffic observed.
Post-fix verification plan: run synthetic canary rollout test against staging with deliberate probe retries to validate pin TTL invariance.
